name: Kashubian

ancestors.notes: Descent from Proto-Slavic (West Slavic, Lechitic / Pomeranian subgroup).
Closely related Lechitic neighbour and roofing standard; sometimes classified as a dialect but has official regional-language status in Poland.
German (Low German) adstrate: centuries under Prussia/Pomerania; very heavy lexical influence.

notes: Kashubian (Kaszëbsczi jãzëk), West Slavic language/dialect spoken in Pomerania, Poland. Official regional language since 2005. Nasal vowel ą /ɔ̃/, schwa ë /ə/. Digraphs sz, cz, rz, dż precede single letters. Significant German loanword influence. Open questions from Hopkins (2001: xi): his table of the official orthography gives ⟨é⟩ = /e/ rather than /ɛ/, and his note 4 makes the grave accent a labial glide onset, so ⟨ù⟩ would be /wu/ rather than the /u/ mapped here.

sources.author: Hopkins, Paul Stanley
sources.title: The phonological structure of the Kashubian word
sources.notes: The 'Guide to Kashubian Orthography' table maps IPA to the official 1995 orthography; its note 4 states that the grave accent marks a labial glide onset to /o/ and /u/.

stress.notes: Kashubian (csb) generally follows the Polish penultimate stress pattern, though some dialects show initial stress. Diacritics ë é ó ô ù mark vowel quality. Source: Stone (1993), Kashubian; Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kashubian_language
